neighbours.label: Words that assess how complete a recovery from illness or disaster is (recovered fully, a complete recovery, recover completely, persistent fatigue, still recovering), vs 'recover', 'fully' and 'completely' in non-health senses
fire: Two years after the earthquake, the village has yet to recover fully.
With rest and fluids, most children recover completely within a week.
Doctors expect him to make a full recovery after the operation.
Many survivors report lingering fatigue months after the infection cleared.
Her knee never fully healed after the accident.
The coral reef is still recovering from the bleaching event of 2016.
It took the farmers a decade to recover completely from the drought.
Some patients never regain their full strength after a stroke.
quiet: Divers recovered the ship's bell from the wreck in 2016.
The old house was fully renovated before it went on sale.
She read the contract completely before signing it.
Investigators recovered the deleted files from the laptop.
The tank was fully loaded with fuel before the trip.
The kids cleaned their rooms completely before dinner.
Police recovered the stolen paintings from a warehouse.
The parking lot was completely full by nine o'clock.

predictions: Sentences about full, partial or lingering recovery from illness or disaster reach 0.4-0.95; recovering objects, restoring things and finishing tasks completely stay under 0.1.
notes: Card: recovered fully, complete recovery, fully recovered, recover completely, post-viral fatigue, persistent symptoms. Probe: recovered fully from the hurricane 0.956, persistent fatigue 0.641, recovered completely 0.503, complete recovery 0.502, economy recovering 0.451; police recovered the car 0.050, fully restored painting 0.070, finished completely 0.060.
